The Energía Mayakan natural gas pipeline project is expanding rapidly

by Yucatan Times September 8, 2026
written by Yucatan Times September 8, 2026 0 comment
37
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:46
Instaread

MÉRIDA, YUCATÁN — The expansion of the Energía Mayakan natural gas pipeline is progressing rapidly across southeastern Mexico, reaching 65% total completion as Phase II enters commercial operation.

Developed by French energy group ENGIE in partnership with Macquarie Asset Management, the overall project represents an investment exceeding $2 billion. The expansion aims to double the region’s natural gas transportation capacity, increasing flow from 250 million to 567 million cubic feet per day to meet rising electrical, industrial, and commercial demand across Chiapas, Tabasco, Campeche, and Yucatán.

Phase II of the development recently went live, adding roughly 200 kilometers of pipeline along with two new regulation and measurement stations. This milestone provides a direct, reliable natural gas supply to key Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) power generation plants, including the Mérida IV and Valladolid IV combined-cycle facilities.

Once fully complete, the project will span more than 700 kilometers of pipeline running parallel to the system’s existing route, supported by three new compression stations and three measurement stations. Over 4,000 workers are involved in the construction effort.

Yucatán Governor Joaquín Díaz Mena and Campeche Governor Layda Sansores joined CFE leadership and ENGIE executives to inspect the project’s progress. Officials highlighted that the infrastructure will play a transformative role in regional energy stability, reducing energy costs for businesses and helping prevent power outages across the Yucatán Peninsula.

Beyond economic benefits, the modern pipeline infrastructure is designed to reduce methane emissions by up to 40% while preventing approximately 4.6 million tons of carbon dioxide emissions annually by replacing dirtier liquid fuels with cleaner-burning natural gas.

State officials emphasized that securing a guaranteed natural gas supply is critical to attracting domestic and foreign industrial investment to southeastern Mexico, paving the way for long-term economic development.
